title: Finite site comparison preserves counit and projection transposes
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of a finite field of characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, $n\ge1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, with chosen compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,r:\overline X\to Y)$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Absolute separatedness is not required. Use constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], $C_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], $F_f^e=Rr_{e,*}j_!^e$, $F_f^p=Rr_{p,*}j_!^p$, and the specified comparison $B_f:C_YF_f^e\xrightarrow{\sim}F_f^pC_X$ [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence]. Let $G_f^e$ be the ordinary-etale right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and $G_f^p=Rf^!$ the finite transported exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Use the specified pullback, coefficient-unit and tensor comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

On bounded etale inputs with bounded constructible finite-Tor images, the canonical comparison $a_{f,K}:C_XG_f^eK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_f^pC_YK$ induced by the site-comparison unit $K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_{Y,*}C_YK$ (the map $\rho_K$ of [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose]) preserves exceptional counits:
$$\varepsilon^p_{f,C_YK}\circ F_f^p(a_{f,K})\circ B_{f,G_f^eK}=C_Y(\varepsilon^e_{f,K}).$$
For $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, let $P^e_{f,M,K}$ be the proper counit-mate projection [def-kun-projection-formula-map] followed by the open tensor comparison [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor], and let $P^p_{f,C_XM,C_YK}$ be exactly the compactification projection of [def-exchange-projection]; use ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and the finite-Tor category [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. After the specified tensor/pullback identifications,
$$ B_{f,M\otimes f^*K}\circ C_Y(P^e_{f,M,K})=P^p_{f,C_XM,C_YK}\circ(B_{f,M}\otimes1_{C_YK}). $$
Consequently the counit-transpose tensor map $\theta^e_{f,K}$, defined as the adjunct of tensor symmetry followed by $(P^e)^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon^e_{f,A}\otimes1_K$, is carried to the specified $\theta^p_{f,C_YK}$ of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Here inverse projections are used only on their finite-Tor domains where they are isomorphisms. The same adjunction comparison carries the right-adjoint conjugates of compact-support compositors and the counit transposes of compact-support exchanges to the specified pro-etale ones. These identifications preserve identities, refinement, composition, Cartesian base change and further compatible open restriction on bounded-below etale-origin inputs. Every bounded constructible pro-etale input admits an etale origin, and equality of maps between such inputs is reflected by $C_T$; the identifications are independent of that origin.

proof.text:
Set $Z=\overline X$, $C_T=\nu_T^*$ and $a_{f,K}=\rho_K$. Since $Z$ is finite type over the field $k$, [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] supplies a finite integer bound $\dim Z\le D$, with $D\ge0$; for $Z=\varnothing$ take $D=0$. Apply [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose] with this same compactification $(j,r)$ and its specified $B_f$. Its hypotheses are bounded-below $K,J$ and bounded-below $G_f^eK$, all satisfied on the stated bounded domain. Its displayed counit equation is exactly
$$\varepsilon^p_{f,C_YK}F_f^p(a_{f,K})B_{f,G_f^eK}=C_Y(\varepsilon^e_{f,K}).$$
It also gives, for any compatible pair $z_pB_{f,J}=C_Y(z_e)$, the equality $\operatorname{adj}_p(z_p)=a_{f,K}C_X(\operatorname{adj}_e(z_e))$. Retain this equality for the tensor and exchange transposes below; the adjunction is used only on bounded-below etale-origin sources.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; bounded-origin specialization as stated in lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose

proof.text:
First compare the proper projections. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the square of constant-$A$ ringed topoi with vertical arrows $r_e:Z_e\to Y_e$, $r_p:Z_p\to Y_p$ and horizontal arrows $\nu_Z,\nu_Y$. The ring maps are the constant-coefficient identifications and the square is the specified pullback square of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. This is a commuting square of morphisms of ringed topoi; it need not be Cartesian. Its exchange is the direct-image mate $b_{r,E}$, not an unspecified isomorphism, by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Consequently, writing $h_{E,K}:C_Z(E\otimes^Lr_e^*K)\cong C_ZE\otimes^Lr_p^*C_YK$ for tensor and pullback comparison, the cited tensor/exchange identity reads
$$Rr_{p,*}(h_{E,K})\,b_{r,E\otimes^Lr_e^*K}\,C_Y(\pi^e_{r,E,K})=\pi^p_{r,C_ZE,C_YK}(b_{r,E}\otimes1).$$
We use this at $E=j_!^eM$. The ordinary counit-defined projections here are precisely those defining $P^e$ and $P^p$; the cited mate normalization rules out changing either projection by an automorphism.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0E48 (remark-compatible-with-diagram); the ringed-square projection/exchange refinement is lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence

proof.text:
Compare the open tensor maps by [lem-sf-comparison-open-tensor-coherence], applied to $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$, $M$ and $N=r_e^*K$. Its equality identifies $C_Z(\gamma^e_{M,N})$ followed by $e_j$ with $\gamma^p_{C_XM,C_ZN}$ preceded by $e_j\otimes1$, using exactly the specified tensor and pullback comparisons. It has no Tor or boundedness restriction. Now use $B_{f,M}=Rr_{p,*}(e_{j,M})b_{r,j_!^eM}$ from [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence]. Expand $P^e=Rr_{e,*}(\gamma^e)\pi_r^e$ and $P^p=Rr_{p,*}(\gamma^p)\pi_r^p$ as in [def-exchange-projection]. Naturality of $b_r$ moves $Rr_{e,*}(\gamma^e)$ across $b_r$; the open equality replaces $e_j C_Z(\gamma^e)$, and Step 2 replaces $b_r C_Y(\pi_r^e)$. The resulting composite is $Rr_{p,*}(\gamma^p)\pi_r^p(B_{f,M}\otimes1)$. Thus
$$B_{f,M\otimes^Lf^*K}\,C_Y(P^e_{f,M,K})=P^p_{f,C_XM,C_YK}(B_{f,M}\otimes1).$$
The pullback-composition identifications $j^*r^*=f^*$ agree with the tensor identifications by the monoidal composition clause of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons].

proof.text: On $M\in D^b_c$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}$, [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] makes both of the named projections in Step 3 invertible. Multiplying that equality on the appropriate sides by their inverses identifies their inverse maps as well. For $M=G_f^eA_Y$ in the stated bounded constructible domain, form the defining composite for $\theta^e$: symmetry, inverse projection, counit at $A_Y$ tensored with $1_K$, then the left unitor. Step 1 identifies the counit, and Step 3 identifies the inverse projection. The symmetry, coefficient-unit and unitor agree under comparison by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], including the monoidal pullback comparison. Therefore the resulting map $z_p:F_f^pC_X(f_e^*K\otimes^LG_f^eA_Y)\to C_YK$ satisfies $z_pB_f=C_Y(z_e)$, after $a_{f,A_Y}$ on the dualizing factor. Apply the transpose identity in Step 1: $a_{f,K}C_X(\theta^e_{f,K})$ is exactly $\theta^p_{f,C_YK}$ with that factor identified. This proves agreement with the specified counit-transpose map of [def-pur-co-smoothness], on precisely the domains where its inverse projection is defined.

proof.text: For a compact-support composition map $\alpha:F_gF_f\to F_{gf}$, its right-adjoint conjugate is determined by composing $\alpha$ with the counit, by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. The composition equality for $B$ in [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence] identifies this left-hand map on the two sites. Step 1 identifies each counit, so [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (2),(3) identifies its conjugate under $a_{gf}$ and $a_fa_g$, with the composite-adjunction comparisons inserted. The identical argument with $\alpha$ replaced by a refinement comparison identifies the refinement conjugates. More explicitly the two candidate right-hand arrows have the same adjoint: apply the corresponding compact-support map and then the same identified counit. The injectivity of the adjunction bijection makes them equal. Pasting with a second composition or refinement gives the same equality by the pasting formulas (1),(2); the identity clause (4) gives the identity case. Thus the comparisons preserve the actual chosen composition/refinement arrows, including all their pasted instances.

proof.text: For an arbitrary Cartesian base change, [lem-pur-co-smooth-exchange-transport] identifies the actual compactification exchanges: in its notation $T_LC_{Y'}(\operatorname{Ex}^e)=\operatorname{Ex}^pS_L$. It assumes only bounded-below etale input and the supplied compactification, and puts no separatedness condition on the base-change morphism. [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] gives invertibility, identities and horizontal/vertical pasting for the etale exchanges; hence the displayed comparison also identifies the inverses on etale-origin inputs. For example, the map transposed to the dualizing base-change arrow is $v^*\varepsilon^e_{f,A}\circ(\operatorname{Ex}^e)^{-1}$ followed by the coefficient-unit identification, as in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Replacing the inverse exchange by this equality and the counit by Step 1 gives the specified pro-etale defining composite. Step 1 identifies its transpose. More generally the same conclusion holds for the counit transposes of exchanges themselves by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (1)--(3), without requiring their inverses. Applying those pasting formulas to a pasted exchange proves compatibility with further Cartesian base change. For open restrictions, the restriction equality and pasting of [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence] apply to these same factors, so the construction also commutes with every further compatible open restriction. Projection compatibility in these squares is the proper tensor/exchange identity of Step 2 and the open tensor identity of Step 3.

proof.text: Finally [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] (ii) gives an etale origin for each bounded constructible pro-etale input. If $(J,\lambda:C_TJ\cong N)$ and $(J',\lambda':C_TJ'\cong N)$ are two choices, full faithfulness in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] gives a unique arrow $u:J\to J'$ with $C_Tu=(\lambda')^{-1}\lambda$. The same assertion for the inverse shows $u$ is an isomorphism. All the comparisons used above are natural in their inputs, so their naturality square at $u$ says exactly that conjugating the maps by $\lambda$ or by $\lambda'$ gives the same map on $N$. For several inputs apply this argument in each variable. Faithfulness reflects each equality of maps between etale origins; existence of origins transfers the verified equalities to bounded constructible pro-etale inputs. This proves independence of origins and finishes the coherence assertions without invoking an exceptional adjunction on the whole ambient unbounded pro-etale category.
